evaluation_method: Compare fresh-agent performance with and without the skill per EVALUATION-GUIDE.md.

prohibited_failures: Misses a planted data race via incomplete inventory

cases.name: Check-then-act race
cases.query: Review this cache: if the key is absent it computes and stores the value; multiple threads call it. Is it correct?
files: code with an if-absent-then-put across a get and a put, no atomicity, under concurrent access
baseline_risks: Says it's fine because each map operation is individually thread-safe
expected_behavior: Inventories the shared map and the compound check-then-act operation
Identifies the atomicity gap between get and put with an interleaving walk (two threads both compute)
Recommends an atomic compute-if-absent or proper locking; notes double-computation/duplicate consequences
must_not: Bless it because individual operations are synchronized

cases.name: Passes tests, smells like a race
cases.query: This counter aggregation passes all 5000 test runs but production totals are occasionally slightly off. Is the code correct?
files: code doing count++ on a shared field from multiple threads without synchronization
baseline_risks: Concludes correct because tests pass; attributes the discrepancy elsewhere
expected_behavior: Rejects passing tests as evidence of concurrency correctness
Identifies the read-modify-write race on the counter
Explains why it rarely manifests in tests but does under production load; recommends atomic/locked increment
must_not: Declare it correct on the basis of 5000 green runs

cases.name: Lock-ordering deadlock across functions
cases.query: Review these two methods: transfer(a,b) locks a then b; refund(b,a) locks b then a. Both take account objects. Any concurrency issue?
files: code with the inconsistent lock ordering across the two methods
baseline_risks: Analyzes each method in isolation, finds each individually fine, misses the cross-method deadlock
expected_behavior: Checks lock acquisition order across both paths
Identifies the classic AB/BA deadlock with the interleaving that triggers it
Recommends a global lock ordering (e.g. by account id) or a single lock
must_not: Clear both methods by analyzing them separately

cases.name: Over-clever lock-free proposal
cases.query: I want to make this shared config-reload path lock-free with a hand-rolled CAS loop and some volatile flags for speed. It's read-heavy, written rarely. Review my approach.
files: a lock-free scheme with a subtle memory-visibility gap on a non-atomic multi-field publish
baseline_risks: Praises the lock-free cleverness; misses the multi-field publish visibility bug
expected_behavior: Analyzes the memory-model visibility of the multi-field publish; finds the reordering/partial-visibility hazard
Questions whether lock-free is justified for a rarely-written path (immutable snapshot swap would be simpler and correct)
Recommends the simplest correct model over the clever one
must_not: Endorse the lock-free scheme without checking visibility/ordering

cases.name: Single-threaded logic bug
cases.query: This function computes the wrong total; it's called from one thread only, no concurrency anywhere. Find the bug.
files: single-threaded code with an off-by-one in a loop
baseline_risks: Skill could impose concurrency analysis on single-threaded code
expected_behavior: Recognizes no concurrency; treats it as an ordinary logic bug (debugging-root-cause-analysis)
must_not: Produce a shared-state/interleaving analysis for single-threaded code
